summary.headline: ICICI Bank Q2 FY27 PAT rose 20.1% YoY to ₹14,843 crore, but NIM fell to 4.18% on FCNR(B) mix, with management guiding to a Q3 trough.
summary.overview: Q2 FY27 profit before tax excluding treasury grew 23.4% YoY to ₹19,954 crore and PAT grew 20.1% to ₹14,843 crore, with standalone RoE of 16.6%. Net interest margin fell to 4.18% from 4.36% in Q1 (4.28% ex-tax-refund interest), which management attributed to FCNR(B) inflows, lower CASA mix and a larger overseas book. Total loans grew 30% YoY and deposits 27.1%, both flattered by about $10 billion of FCNR(B)-linked leverage; ex-leverage loans grew 24.1%. Asset quality stayed clean, with net NPA at 0.30% and the provision coverage ratio at 75%.

financial_highlights.change: vs 4.36% in Q1 FY27 (4.28% ex tax-refund interest) and 4.30% in Q2 FY26
vs ₹914 crore in Q2 FY26; 0.20% of average advances
vs gain of ₹151 crore in Q1 FY27

segments.name: Retail and rural
segments.commentary: Retail and rural book grew 14.8% YoY and 3.2% QoQ, now 43% of total portfolio including non-fund. Mortgages +15.3% YoY, personal loans +16.6%, jewel loans +79.4% YoY (+4.5% QoQ), credit cards -9.7% YoY and -0.2% QoQ.

segments.name: Corporate and business banking
segments.commentary: Domestic corporate loans grew 30.6% YoY and 10.4% QoQ; business banking grew 33.8% YoY and 11.1% QoQ. Management attributed corporate growth to working capital, capex, and bond/ECB-to-bank shift. 73.2% of corporate book rated A and above.

segments.name: Overseas and international branches
segments.commentary: Overseas loans were 7.8% of the book. FCNR(B) leverage loans sit in overseas branches, which earn about 1% margin versus 4%-plus domestic, and this mix shift is a key driver of margin compression.

guidance_outlook: Management expects a further marginal NIM decline in Q3 FY27 as the full-quarter FCNR(B) impact flows through averages, with margins rising from Q4 even at current policy rates.
Management's house view is two more repo hikes of 25 bps each, taking repo to about 6%; repo-linked loans (57% of domestic book) reprice faster than deposits.
Normalised credit cost is about 50 bps of advances after adjusting for one-off corporate recoveries, FCNR(B) standard asset provisions and KCC seasonality.
Agri standard-asset provision of ₹1,283 crore (made in Q3 FY26) may be reversed after RBI review; management expects an update within 1-2 quarters.
No explicit loan or deposit growth target; management declined to forecast credit growth moderation.
capex_capacity: Branch network at 7,656 with 145 branches added in H1 FY27; 12,143 ATMs and cash recycling machines at September 30, 2026.
Average liquidity coverage ratio for the quarter was about 126%; management noted excess liquidity to be deployed over the next two quarters.

FCNR(B) deposits of about $18 billion mobilised under RBI swap facility; about $10 billion leveraged, $3.6 billion via partner-bank leverage and about $4 billion retail self-funded; landed cost about 6.5% including hedging.
ICICI Life bought an additional 2% stake for ₹1,470 crore in the quarter.
demand_pricing: Period-end deposits grew 27.1% YoY and 11.8% QoQ; ex-FCNR(B) deposits grew 17.0% YoY and 3.1% QoQ. Average CASA deposits grew 10.7% YoY.
Cost of deposits rose to 4.50% from 4.41% in Q1 and 4.64% a year earlier; CASA mix decline cost about 9-10 bps of margin.
Management said competitive intensity is unchanged, not materially higher QoQ.
Gold loan growth is from a small base, is now urban-led, and sequential growth slowed as processes were aligned with new RBI guidelines.
Credit card decline is attributed to festive-season spend timing; management expects growth from Q3 FY27.

qa_highlights.question: What drove the 18 bp NIM decline and where does it stabilise?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed the fall from 4.28% (ex-tax-refund) to 4.18% to FCNR(B) inflows, lower CASA ratio, higher overseas book share and retail term deposits. Full impact lands in Q3, with margins rising from Q4.

qa_highlights.question: How much of the $18 billion FCNR(B) was deployed and where?
qa_highlights.answer: Part was used to repay bulk deposits and part funded Q2 loan growth; the balance will be deployed over the next two quarters. Management declined to quantify the bulk deposit reduction.

qa_highlights.question: Impact of the proposed IRDAI insurance distribution guidelines on fee income?
qa_highlights.answer: Bancassurance is under 1% of total income and about 5% of fees. Management said it sells only ICICI Group insurance products and the impact will be minimal.

qa_highlights.question: Why did the Q2 treasury turn into a loss?
qa_highlights.answer: The ₹230 crore loss reflected G-sec yield increases on the fixed income portfolio (bond yields rose about 44 bps in the quarter). Management gave no outlook on treasury or bond yields.

qa_highlights.question: What were the Q2 slippages and write-offs?
qa_highlights.answer: Gross NPA additions were ₹4,833 crore (retail and rural ₹3,709 crore; corporate and business banking ₹1,124 crore). Recoveries and upgrades were ₹3,620 crore and write-offs ₹1,592 crore, leaving net additions of ₹1,213 crore.

qa_highlights.question: Is corporate loan growth sustainable, and is it temporary FCNR parking?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said there is no temporary parking. Corporate growth reflects client demand, a base effect and a shift from bonds and ECBs, and there is no targeted retail-corporate mix.

risks_watch: NIM trough in Q3 FY27 from full-quarter FCNR(B) drag, with recovery dependent on Q4 reversal and deposit repricing.
Corporate-heavy growth from leveraged FCNR(B) funding; about $10 billion of loans sit in overseas branches and the tenor and unwind of this book is key.
Pending RBI review of agri standard-asset provisions (₹1,283 crore) and possible reversal; El Niño and drought conditions could affect the agri book.
RBI foreign exchange risk reserve mandate may moderate FX hedging volumes and client documentation requirements.
Proposed IRDAI distribution guidelines and any UPI MDR changes; management says impact is minimal.
Credit card book shrinking YoY; management expects Q3 festive-season recovery.
Operating cost growth of 8.5% YoY versus fee and NII growth, with employee costs up 13.5% YoY.
summary.management_tone: Confident on franchise growth and earnings, but cautious and evasive on forward metrics: management declined to give NIM, credit growth, treasury, bulk deposit and FCNR-impact numbers, saying these are dynamic or theoretical.
key_quotes: The full impact would largely get reflected in the third quarter, after which we expect the margins to start moving up, even based on the current level of policy rates.
We do not give a forecast.
Whatever changes happen will have minimal impact on the Bank.
Frankly, I would say that we have done better than what we originally thought we would do when this scheme started.

adds.what: 145 branches added in H1 FY27 (network at 7,656); 12,143 ATMs and cash recycling machines

growth.why: No explicit loan or deposit growth target; management guides only a marginal NIM dip in Q3 then rising NIM from Q4, with credit cost held at about 50 bps, and backs growth with excess liquidity and a branch network rather than specific capacity or orders.
